sundar.57.cau1: Hearing the letter, Rāvaṇa was afraid at heart, but with a smile on his face he said for all to hear: Lying on the ground, he would grasp the sky with his hand. This is mere big talk from the younger ascetic.
sundar.57.cau2: Śuka said: My lord, every word of it is true; set aside your proud nature and understand it. Put away your anger and hear what I say: my lord, give up your enmity with Śrī Rāma.
sundar.57.cau3: Śrī Rāma's nature is very gentle, though he is king of all the worlds. The moment you meet him the Lord will show you grace; he will not keep a single offence of yours in his heart.
sundar.57.cau4: Hand Sītā over to Śrī Rāma; my lord, do this much that I ask. When Śuka spoke of giving Sītā back, the wicked Rāvaṇa kicked him.
sundar.57.cau5: Śuka bowed his head to Rāvaṇa's feet and went to where Śrī Rāma, the ocean of mercy, was. He bowed to him and told his story, and by Śrī Rāma's grace he regained his own true state.
sundar.57.cau6: Pārvatī, by the curse of the sage Agastya he had become a demon; before that he had been a wise sage. Bowing again and again at Śrī Rāma's feet, the sage went back to his hermitage.
sundar.57.do57: The dull ocean would not heed the entreaty, and three days went by. Then Śrī Rāma said in anger: Without fear there is no love.
sundar.58.cau1: Lakṣmaṇa, bring the bow and arrows; let me dry up the ocean with the fire of an arrow. Entreaty to the wicked, love for the crooked, fine counsel to one who is a miser by nature,
sundar.58.cau2: talk of wisdom to one wrapped up in attachment, praise of dispassion to the very greedy, talk of calm to the wrathful and the story of Śrī Hari to the lustful: all these bear the same fruit as seed sown in barren ground.
sundar.58.cau3: With these words Śrī Rāma strung his bow, and this view pleased Lakṣmaṇa. The Lord fitted a terrible arrow, and flames rose within the ocean's heart.
sundar.58.cau4: Crocodiles, serpents and shoals of fish were thrown into distress. When the Ocean knew that the creatures were burning, he filled a golden platter with gems of many kinds and, setting aside his pride, came in the form of a brāhmaṇa.
sundar.58.do58: However much one waters it, with endless care, a banana plant bears fruit only when it is cut. Listen, Garuḍa: the base do not heed a humble request; they bend only when rebuked.
sundar.59.cau1: The Ocean, afraid, took hold of the Lord's feet: Forgive all my faults, my Lord. Sky, wind, fire, water and earth, my Lord, are by their very nature dull in what they do.
sundar.59.cau2: Impelled by you, māyā brought them forth for the work of creation; so all the scriptures sing. Whatever the Lord has commanded for each, each finds happiness in keeping to it.
sundar.59.cau3: My Lord, you did well to teach me a lesson; yet the bounds were set by you as well. A drum, the unlettered, a śūdra, an animal and a woman: all of these are meant to receive instruction.
sundar.59.cau4: Through the Lord's might I shall dry up, and the army will get across, but there is no glory for me in that. The Lord's command cannot be set aside, the Vedas sing; whatever pleases you, I will do it at once.
sundar.59.do59: Hearing these most humble words, the compassionate Lord smiled and said: Dear one, tell me the way by which the monkey army may cross.
sundar.60.cau1: My Lord, the monkeys Nīla and Nala are two brothers who received a sage's blessing in childhood. At their touch, even massive mountains will float upon the ocean through your glory.
sundar.60.cau2: I too, holding the Lord's greatness in my heart, will help as far as my strength allows. Have the ocean bridged in this manner, my Lord, so that the three worlds may sing this fair renown.
sundar.60.cau3: With this arrow, my Lord, slay the wicked men who live on my northern shore, heaps of sin that they are. Hearing of the pain in the Ocean's heart, the compassionate Śrī Rāma, steadfast in battle, took it away at once.
sundar.60.cau4: Seeing Śrī Rāma's mighty strength and valour, the Ocean rejoiced and was at ease. He told the Lord the whole story, bowed at his feet and departed.
sundar.60.cha1: The Ocean went to his own home, and this counsel pleased Śrī Rāma. This story washes away the impurity of the Kali age; the servant Tulasīdāsa has sung it as far as his understanding allows. The virtues of Śrī Rāma are a home of happiness; they put doubt to rest and destroy sorrow. Foolish mind, let go of every hope and every reliance, and sing and hear them always.
sundar.60.do60: Singing the praises of Śrī Rāma brings every blessing. Whoever listens to them with reverence crosses the ocean of worldly existence without a boat.
